framework.note: Central: CIRP is the rescue mechanism for commercial entities; defines trigger, initiation by creditor/company/operational creditor, and NCLT jurisdiction.

framework.ref: IBC 2016, Section 21–35 (CIRP process: Interim Resolution Professional, Committee of Creditors, timeline)
framework.note: Central: governs the 30-day interim window, CoC formation, 180-day resolution plan evaluation, and extension provisions.
Central: threshold of default (₹1 lakh), default definition, plea by corporate debtor vs. creditor; creditor standing and verification.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy (Application to Adjudicating Authority) Rules, 2016
framework.note: Central: NCLT procedure, plea filing, notice, admission order, appointment timeline for insolvency professional.
Central: listed entity must disclose material events (including CIRP filing) to stock exchange within 30 minutes of occurrence or start of trading day.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (Insolvency Professional) Regulations, 2016
framework.note: Procedural: credentialing, ethics, conduct, and liability of appointed insolvency professional; determines professional capacity and standards.

framework.ref: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) Act, 1997 & Licences
framework.note: Sector-specific: telecom spectrum, licences, and services obligations may be affected by CIRP; licencees must meet financial covenants; DoT/TRAI may intervene on licence terms.
Central: upon CIRP admission, automatic moratorium prohibits recovery actions against corporate debtor; exceptions for secured creditors in certain cases.

Comparative: companies may exit CIRP via resolution plan approval by CoC (66% by value) or pursue Companies Act Section 230–232 settlement; telecom entities with ongoing licences may pursue hybrid paths.

headline: Reliance Communications initiates Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process
sum: Reliance Communications Limited disclosed to NSE a Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process filing, indicating formal commencement of IBC proceedings. Exact creditor claims, debt quantum, and appointment of insolvency professional to be confirmed from NCLT/IBBI registry and company's detailed disclosures.
detail: Reliance Communications Limited notified the NSE of a Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) filing on 24 June 2026. CIRP is the formal rescue mechanism under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, initiated following a petition (typically by a creditor or the company) to the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT). For a telecom operator of RCOM's scale and leverage, this represents formal entry into the statutory 180-day (extendable) resolution window. Critical outstanding details include the exact petitioner identity, admitted debt quantum, appointed insolvency professional, and creditor composition.
